question: A project lead pastes the same 40-page requirements document into every new chat instead of storing it anywhere. What is the greatest concern with this approach?
options: A) Each re-paste spends both window space and usage allowance that storing the document once would save.
B) The document will be copied into other people's projects across her organisation without her consent.
C) Claude will answer only from the closing pages of the document and silently ignore everything before.
D) Claude will refuse to accept a document of that size and will ask her to shorten it before continuing.
correct_answers: A) Each re-paste spends both window space and usage allowance that storing the document once would save.
explanations: Correct. The document consumes a large share of the conversation's working memory every time, and the repeated processing draws on her usage budget for no added benefit.
Incorrect. Pasting into her own chat does not propagate the document to colleagues' workspaces.
Incorrect. Claude does not restrict itself to the final pages; the real exposure is cost and space, not truncation by position.
Incorrect. A document of that size is readable; the cost is in the space and allowance it consumes, not a refusal.
